title: Operator-encoded degradation contracts & tenant fallback budgets — PRD updates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: During the 2025-10 coldstart/autoscale incident, operators applied a manual sequence of mitigations (cache priming, burst pool activation, and per-tenant request throttles) that restored throughput but lacked a declarative, repeatable contract. This ticket updates the Serving PRD to convert key postmortem actions into product requirements: a machine-readable "degradation contract" format, tenant-level fallback budgets that the control plane can enforce automatically, and synthetic acceptance gates to validate behavior before rollout.

Goal: Reduce mean time to safe-degradation by automating the runbook steps that were executed ad-hoc during the incident. Provide clear customer-visible degradation guarantees and operator tooling so that degraded-mode behavior is consistent, auditable, and safe for multi-tenant Dedicated/Private deployments.

Deliverables (PRD-level): 1) Specification for a Degradation Contract schema (JSON/YAML) that encodes: SLO trigger thresholds, fallback model variants, allowed throttling bands, KV-cache-regen priorities, and explicit rollback criteria. 2) Tenant Fallback Budget model: per-tenant budget units (requests/sec-equivalent) that can be consumed during degraded periods with configurable notification policies. 3) Console and API surfaces to author and preview degradation contracts, and to view current budget consumption. 4) Synthetic gating harness: a suite of deterministic tests (coldstart/regen/eviction scenarios) that must pass in staging before any runtime rollout that changes fallback behavior. 5) Observable signals and dashboards required by the PRD (SLIs, SLO gates, budget burn-rate alerts, audit trail).

Why this is different: Existing PRDs cover rollback/runbook content in prose. This change mandates machine-encodable contracts plus tenant-level economics so runtime can reason about trade-offs automatically and provide predictable customer outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Contract schema v1 is defined with examples covering: model fallback, throttling bands, cache-priority, and rollback conditions
APIs exist to attach a Degradation Contract to a deployment and to query effective contract evaluation for a given request at runtime
Console UX mockups for authoring and previewing contracts reviewed and approved by Design
Tenant Fallback Budget API and storage model implemented with per-tenant read/write and audit logs
Synthetic gating harness includes at least three deterministic scenarios (coldstart surge, KV cache regen stall, kernel-latency spike) and can be run in CI against staging clusters
Dashboards and alerts for budget burn-rate, contract-trigger events, and canary rollback recommendations created and validated by SRE
On-call playbook updated with automated remediation steps; playbook references the exact contract fields to mutate during incidents
Security review completed for the contract editor API and storage; any secrets or tenant-scoped configs are KMS-backed
scope: In scope: PRD text/specification, API surface definition, console mocks, acceptance criteria, synthetic test scenarios, SLI/SLO definitions, operator runbook mapping
Out of scope: full runtime implementation, tenant billing integration, and integrations with third-party orchestration (will be follow-up tickets)
success_metrics: Reduce operator manual intervention steps during first 30 minutes of an autoscale/coldstart incident by >= 60% (measured via runbook audit)
95th percentile time-to-stable-throughput after a synthetic coldstart test reduced by 30% in staging
>90% of degraded-mode rollouts in canary pass synthetic gating before reaching 10% traffic
Customer-visible error-rate during controlled degraded-mode experiments stays within contract thresholds for >= 90% of tenants
comments: 2025-11-18 - Scoped kickoff with SRE (J. Morales) and Runtime eng (K. Gupta); agreed to target schema-first approach; SRE to own alert definitions.
2025-11-20 - Design sync: initial console wireframes capture intent to show live budget burn-rate and a 'simulate' button to run synthetic scenarios against a contract.
2025-11-25 - Engineering input: ENG estimates 8 points for PRD->API contract prototype; recommends contract be opt-in for Dedicated and Private initially.
2025-11-27 - Security: flagged that contract editor must not expose tenant secrets; PM added KMS-backed storage requirement to PRD.
2025-11-30 - Draft PRD published to Confluence for review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DegradationContracts-PRD (private).
2025-12-01 - PM review complete; consolidated feedback into acceptance criteria and added synthetic-gating must-run CI requirement. Next: handoff to eng to produce API stub and spec.
notes_for_engineering: Contract evaluation must be deterministic and versioned: include schema version and a migration plan for unknown fields
Budget model should support both absolute units and proportional throttles (eg. 100 req-equivalents or 10% of normal capacity)
APIs need RBAC: only operators and designated tenant admins can mutate live contracts; console should show effective policy provenance
Synthetic harness will need deterministic traffic generator and a 'timewarp' facility to simulate long-tail token generation quickly
Telemetry: emit contract_evaluated events with fields: contract_id, tenant_id, decision_reason, budget_delta, and trace_id
Fallback payloads: define a stable contract field for 'user-facing message' so customer apps can surface consistent messaging during degraded mode
